metadata.summary: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to profile the transcriptional landscape of ventricular tissue in a Sprague-Dawley rat model of myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). Two groups were analyzed: an I/R control group and a group treated with the pro-lymphangiogenic polymeric formulation PD-DN. Ventricular tissues were collected from both groups at three time points post-injury — 3, 5, and 7 days — to capture the temporal dynamics of cardiac repair. Single-cell suspensions were processed using the 10x Genomics Chromium platform with Illumina NovaSeq sequencing. Our analysis revealed temporally orchestrated changes in endothelial, immune, and fibroblast cell populations. The data provide insights into how PD-DN-driven lymphangiogenesis reprograms the cardiac microenvironment to facilitate functional recovery.

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

observations.text:
BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate title-abstract screening in systematic reviews, but validation studies typically report sensitivity, specificity, or Cohens kappa -- metrics that are unstable under the low and unbalanced prevalence that characterises most reviews. No previous study has simultaneously combined a medical topic; a hybrid two-stage pipeline (rules + LLM); a three-way classification with a separately sampled uncertain class; stratified sampling with three independent human reviewers; and dual reporting of prevalence-robust coefficients (PABAK and Gwets AC1).

ObjectiveTo validate a two-stage automated screening pipeline (a rule-based Python script followed by a reproducible LLM adjudication of uncertain records) against three independent human reviewers in a medical systematic review on high on-treatment platelet reactivity (HTPR), aspirin resistance, and carotid plaque. The primary validation target is the Stage 1 automatic-exclusion decision (670/904 records), which is the workload the pipeline is designed to take off the human reviewer.

MethodsFrom 904 screened records (Stage 1: 131 INCLUDE, 670 EXCLUDE, 94 UNCERTAIN; Stage 2 LLM via API, temperature = 0: 11 INCLUDE, 83 EXCLUDE), a stratified sample of 185 records (50 per Stage 1 stratum + 35 Stage 2; seed = 42) was judged independently and blind to the automated labels by three physicians: E.P. (pipeline designer), D.C. and P.P.B. (both external to the thesis project). Concordance was quantified with sensitivity, specificity, PABAK (q = 3 throughout), Gwets AC1, work saved over sampling (WSS), and number needed to read (NNR) -- AI versus each reviewer and between reviewers -- overall and by stratum. Majority labels (2 of 3) are reported as a supplementary panel; they do not replace pairwise tables as the primary reference for sensitivity.

ResultsOn the primary target, Stage1-EXCLUDE concordance was PABAK = AC1 = 1.000 versus E.P. (48/48) and versus D.C. (50/50), and PABAK = 0.940 / AC1 = 0.959 versus Berti (48/50 EXCLUDE, 2 UNCERTAIN). That stratum is 670/904 records (74.1%). Pairwise human agreement was highest between the two external readers (Costazza vs Berti: PABAK = 0.854, AC1 = 0.881) and lower when E.P. was one of the pair (0.703 / 0.774 vs Costazza; 0.621 / 0.702 vs Berti). AI versus each human remained poor (PABAK 0.225 / 0.205 / 0.222). Majority labels on 185 records were 146 EXCLUDE / 27 UNCER-TAIN / 4 INCLUDE / 8 NO_MAJORITY. The machine labelled INCLUDE 0 of the 4 majority-INCLUDE records (74, 75, 76, 80). Overall sensitivity was 0.800 versus E.P. (8/10; false negatives 623, 712), 0.500 versus D.C. (1/2; false negative 76), and 0.833 versus Berti (5/6; false negative 76). Versus majority the false-negative count is 1 (record 76); records 623 and 712 are majority EXCLUDE. Stage1-INCLUDE sensitivity of 1.000 is tautological. WSS = 74.1% describes the exclusion stratum only.

ConclusionsWhat this study validates, now with three independent physicians, is automatic exclusion at Stage 1. Fine classification of INCLUDE records is not validated: humans do not agree on which residual records are INCLUDE (triple INCLUDE intersection = record 74 only), Stage 2 missed most of the few human INCLUDE labels it received, and the machine recovered none of the four majority-INCLUDE records. Domain-familiarity as an explanation of INCLUDE divergence remains a hypothesis, not a measured variable.

observations.text:
PurposeOpen-source vision-language models (VLMs) can be locally deployed without external internet access. This study aimed to evaluate the slice-level lesion-detection performance of multiple general-purpose and medical-purpose open-source VLMs for brain metastases on contrast-enhanced (CE) MRI, and to assess their accuracy in characterizing detailed imaging features on lesion-positive images.

Materials and MethodsOne hundred lesion-positive axial CE T1-weighted images and 100 matched lesion-negative images from 100 patients were analyzed using eight evaluable VLMs: five general-purpose VLMs-InternVL3-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, MiniCPM-V-4.5, DeepSeek-VL2-tiny, and Phi-3.5-vision-instruct-and three medical-purpose VLMs-MedGemma-4B-it, LLaVA-Med v1.5, and HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B. Lesion-detection performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy. On lesion-positive images, accuracy was evaluated for lesion count, laterality, anatomic location, enhancement pattern, necrosis, and mass effect. Balanced accuracy was reported with patient-level cluster bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Models were compared using the Friedman test and paired patient-level permutation tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Secondary outcomes were compared with majority-class baselines using exact McNemar tests. A revised prompt was tested post hoc.

ResultsThe median age of the study patients was 65 years (IQR, 59.0-70.0), and 58 patients were male (58.0%). MiniCPM-V-4.5 showed significantly higher balanced accuracy (80.5%; 95% CI, 75.0-85.5) than all other models (FDR-adjusted P < 0.001). Seven of the eight models showed predicted-positive rates of 81-100%, and 70.8% (17/24) of responses to synthetic control images without anatomic content were classified as lesion-positive. With the revised prompt, balanced accuracy increased from 59.5% to 77.0% in HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B and from 51.5% to 68.5% in InternVL3-8B. No model significantly outperformed the majority-class baseline for enhancement pattern or for mass effect.

ConclusionThis slice-level technical benchmark demonstrated variable lesion-detection performance of open-source VLMs for brain metastasis in an image-only setting, with most models showing a strong positive-response tendency.
observations.title: Benchmarking Open-Source Vision-Language Models for Brain Metastasis Assessment on Single-Slice Contrast-Enhanced MRI

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

observations.title: Autoimmune-like T Cell Responses Drive Atherosclerotic Plaque Instability

observations.text:
Identifying progressive dementia during its prodromal stage is a challenging yet critical task for healthcare providers. Traditional clinical assessments are often not sensitive enough to detect warning signs of cognitive decline. Machine learning (ML) methods have shown promise in modeling clinical trajectories associated with neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimers disease (AD). Validation of these models forecasting abilities, however, is widely lacking in the literature. To address this gap, we established a longitudinal cohort from the National Alzheimers Coordinating Center (n = 15,727) comprising individuals who were cognitively normal (CN) or had mild cognitive impairment (MCI) at baseline. Cognitive status and clinical observations collected over up to 10 visits were used to train several ML classifiers. We employed the gradient-boosted tree ensemble method XGBoost with a custom feature-engineering pipeline. On non-imputed data, our models achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.9447 [0.9417-0.9476] and PR-AUC of 0.8554 [0.8497-0.8611] for the CN[->]MCI task, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9059 [0.8983-0.9134] and PR-AUC of 0.9214 [0.9156-0.9272] for the MCI[->]AD task. In a lead-time forecasting analysis spanning mean follow-up periods of 56.1 months (range, 9.1-214.1) for CN[->]MCI and 42.7 months (range, 9.1-126.1) for MCI[->]AD, the non-imputed models detected future progression before diagnosis in 29.58% [28.29%-30.87%] of CN[->]MCI progressors and 22.41% [21.36%-23.46%] of MCI[->]AD progressors. Among these individuals, the mean lead time was 33.04 months [32.52-33.56] and 17.95 months [17.71-18.19], respectively. False alarm rates among non-progressors were 12.6% [11.5%-13.7%] and 20.0% [18.4%-21.6%], respectively. These findings suggest that longitudinal machine learning models can identify future cognitive decline before diagnosis, indicating clinical utility for early dementia risk stratification.

Author summaryAlzheimers disease (AD) is a progressive and currently incurable neurodegenerative disorder that remains highly difficult to diagnose during its early stages. While modern early-stage dementia research relies on advanced neuroimaging, the high cost of these tests excludes many vulnerable communities. We designed our study to advance scalable, low-cost diagnostic alternatives that can identify individuals at significant risk of cognitive decline, ensuring faster access to emerging therapies.

We examined trajectories of cognitive decline in 15,727 adults (mean age = 71.45 years, SD = 9.06) who had between 2 and 10 follow-up visits. Using 37 demographic, behavioral, clinical, and genetic variables, we modeled cognitively stable and declining trajectories using the XGBoost algorithm. Additionally, we evaluated the models ability to forecast future diagnoses and the impact of longitudinal imputation.

Our models performed well in both classification tasks (AUC-ROC [≥] 0.90).

Imputation did not substantively alter the classifiers performance. In forecasting diagnosis conversion, the models raised alarms before the recorded conversion visit in a subset of progressors, with non-imputed models yielding longer net lead times than imputed models in AD forecasting. This work describes a strategy for handling mixed-length temporal dimensions in longitudinal cohorts and evaluates its prognostic ability.
observations.title: Forecasting Alzheimer's disease progression using non-imaging clinical features and XGBoost

metadata.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) exhibit limited efficacy against lung cancer brain metastases, often resulting in rapid and inevitable resistance. However, the unique mechanisms driving this brain microenvironment-specific therapeutic failure remain elusive. Here, utilizing in vivo orthotopic models and single-cell RNA sequencing, we reveal that targeted therapy induces a distinct, metabolically hyperactive senescent cell subpopulation that drives rapid EGFR-TKI tolerance in brain metastasis. We identify the molecular chaperone CRYAB as an indispensable driver specifically upregulated within this senescent persister state. Mechanistically, CRYAB physically interacts with VDAC2 at the outer mitochondrial membrane, promoting endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria tethering and calcium influx. This CRYAB-VDAC2 axis orchestrates adaptive mitochondrial fission, hyperactivating oxidative metabolism while simultaneously shielding（preventing？） senescent cells from fatal oxidative stress. Genetic or pharmacological blockade of mitochondrial fission completely abolishes CRYAB-mediated therapeutic resistance. Therapeutically, we demonstrate that a 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) dietary intervention acts as a potent in vivo senolytic strategy, directly dismantling the CRYAB-dependent resistance network, eradicating senescent persister cells, and synergistically prolonging overall survival when combined with Osi. Furthermore, high baseline CRYAB expression in pre-treatment primary lung biopsies clinically predicts lower intracranial objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival in a cohort of advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Collectively, our study uncovers a novel CRYAB-VDAC2-mitochondrial fission axis that enforces therapy-induced senescence and highlights 25HC dietary intervention as a highly translatable combinatorial strategy to overcome EGFR-TKI resistance in brain metastasis.

observations.title: CRYAB-driven mitochondrial fission induces senescence to promote adaptive resistance to EGFR-TKI in LUAD brain metastasis

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.title: Spatial genome and transcriptome co-mapping reveals clonal heterogeneity in tumor tissue [RNA-Seq]

observations.text: Human liver microsome (HLM)-based metabolic stability assays are fundamental in early drug discovery, shaping pharmacokinetic profiles and oral bioavailability. However, these experimental assays are labor-intensive and time-consuming, limiting their application in large-scale virtual screening. Computational models can prioritize compounds at scale, yet most are classification-based, leaving quantitative and interpretable prediction of HLM half-life limited. In this study, we developed a quantitative machine learning model for the direct prediction of HLM half-life (T1/2) by integrating 11,790 compounds combining in-house and curated public data. Among various combinations of molecular features and learning algorithms, the XGBoost model with RDKit 2D descriptors achieved the best predictive performance, with an RMSE of 0.507 and an R2 of 0.431 on an independent test set. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified lipophilicity and known metabolic soft-spot features as the primary contributors to the predictions. These results suggest that this quantitative approach provides a practical framework for defining metabolic stability margins, thereby supporting rapid Go/No-go decisions in preclinical drug discovery. The source code, data, and trained model are available at https://github.com/joshua-416/PredHLM.

observations.text: Directed evolution enables the discovery of protein mutants with improved fitness through iterative rounds of selection and has been widely applied to adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid engineering. Machine learning (ML) can augment this process by prioritising mutants for experimental validation, but whether its benefits outweigh the added cost of ML-designed library construction remains unclear. Here, we address this question by considering improvements in manufacturing efficiency of AAV capsids in the context of exosomal encapsulation, which is a technique for improving AAV immunogenicity. We generated a directed evolution dataset comprising 53,974 mutants across three rounds of selection and an independent assessment dataset of 472 ML-designed mutants with detailed profiling. Directed evolution alone yielded a 3-fold improvement, while ML-assisted directed evolution yielded a 41-fold improvement in manufacturing efficiency, demonstrating that ML-assisted directed evolution outperforms directed evolution alone. We show that data quality - specifically the number of selection rounds and the statistical power of mutant counts - has a greater impact on model performance than model architecture. Finally, we provide practical guidance on experimental design and implementation of ML tuning strategies that can augment model performance in protein engineering applications.

metadata.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. Despite upregulation of TGFB1, the rest of the canonical TGF-β pathway was consistently downregulated in MFS, indicating a potential compromise of TGF-β signaling and lack of stimulus for SMC differentiation.

observations.title: Single-cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients With Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-β Signaling

metadata.summary: Fibroblast differentiation into matrix-producing, contractile myofibroblasts is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but whether these changes precede differentiation or arise from the activated phenotype remains unclear. To define when transcriptional remodeling emerges after TGFβ stimulation, we performed bulk RNA-seq on cardiac fibroblasts treated with TGFβ or bFGF for 1, 6, 12, 24, or 48 h. Our transcripomics revealed only 394 genes were differentially expressed at 1 h, but 4,188 DEGs were detected by 6 h, with the total DEG burden peaking at 24 h. These findings support a phased, time-dependent remodeling of the cardiac fibroblast transcriptome in response to TGFβ relative to bFGF in which an initially limited response occurs at 1 h, expands substantially by 6 h, and subsequently encompasses cell cycle regulation, stress responses, developmental- and differentiation-associated programs, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling.

metadata.summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/− mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II–treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/− mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility–HFpEF interactions.

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

metadata.summary: Heart failure (HF) is a growing global health crisis with a persistently poor prognosis, increasingly recognized as an inflammatory disease driven by CD4+ T lymphocytes that promote cardiac fibrosis and stiffness. Current therapies fail to address this immune component effectively. Here, we introduce first-in-class, drug-free Nano-Immuno-Metabolic Modulators (NIMMs) that ameliorate fibrosis by systemically reprogramming macrophage metabolism to curb pro-fibrotic T cell responses. Through high-throughput screening, we identified a lead candidate, NIMM22, which accumulates in the spleen and lymph nodes and potently upregulates macrophage arginase-1 expression. This metabolic shift depletes local L-arginine, suppressing CD4+ T cell effector function and their subsequent recruitment to the heart. NIMM22 treatment alleviated fibrosis and restored cardiac function across multiple murine cardiomyopathy models, including hypertensive and genetic disease. Chronic administration revealed no systemic toxicity or broad immune suppression, a safety profile confirmed in non-human primates. Our work establishes a new paradigm for cargo-free nanotherapeutics that modulate the cardiosplenic axis, offering a targeted, immunotherapy-like strategy with broad potential for treating cardiac and other immune-mediated fibrotic diseases.

observations.text:
ObjectivesTo investigate the association between time spent in NHS Type 1 emergency departments (EDs, consultant led 24-hour services with full resuscitation facilities) and risk of leaving employment and hospitalisation after leaving the department alive up to two years after attendance.

MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using linked administrative data from the NHS Emergency Care Dataset, Hospital Episode Statistics, Census 2021, and mortality records. ED length of stay was categorised from under 2 hours to 12 hours or more. Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to estimate the association between ED length of stay and subsequently leaving employment or being hospitalised over a two-year follow-up period, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical characteristics.

ResultsOur study population comprised 3,347,008 individuals aged 25-64 who attended a Type 1 ED in England between April 2021 and March 2023. For leaving employment, adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) increased from 1.04 (95% CI 1.03-1.06) for stays of 2 to <4 hours to 1.21 (1.17-1.24) for 12 hours or more, compared with stays under 2 hours. A similar but more pronounced gradient was observed for post-discharge hospitalisation, with aHRs rising from 1.06 (1.04-1.07) at 2 to <4 hours to 1.95 (1.91-1.99) for stays of 12 hours or more.

ConclusionsProlonged time spent in the ED is associated with poorer outcomes among working-age employees, including reduced labour market participation and increased hospital use. These findings suggest that long ED stays may have wider and longer-term implications beyond immediate clinical outcomes, including potentially for national labour markets and economic growth.
observations.title: Emergency Department Length of Stay, Employment Status, and Subsequent Risk of Hospitalisation: A survival analysis of linked administrative records in England

metadata.summary: The prevalence of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) is increasing, with growing evidence implicating the intrauterine environment as a critical regulator of fetal brain development. Gestational perturbations such as maternal stress can increase NDD risk; however, the mechanism(s) by which prenatal maternal stress reshape fetal neurodevelopment remain unclear. Accordingly, the objective of my project was to characterize how maternal cold stress exposure during pregnancy disrupts neural stem and progenitor cell (NSPC) developmental programs in the fetus and the impact this has on neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. Pregnant mice were exposed to 4°C for 30 minutes daily from embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5) to E15.5—a critical period of neurodevelopment in the hypothalamus. To assess how maternal cold stress impacts neural stem cell (NSC) behaviours, we employed the neurosphere assay, quantifying the number and size of primary and secondary neurospheres as a measure of NSC proliferation and self-renewal, respectively. Our findings revealed no change in NSC proliferation or self-renewal when comparing control and maternal cold stress male and female neurospheres. However, differentiation of dissociated NSCs revealed that neurons from both sexes had longer axons following maternal cold stress exposure. Interestingly, only male-derived cultures exhibited a significant increase in the number TUJ1+ neurons in response to maternal cold stress exposure, whereas only female-derived maternal cold stress cultures showed enhanced dendritic arborization. To explore the molecular basis of these changes, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on E15.5 fetal hypothalamic NSPCs. Analysis of differentially expressed genes uncovered basal sex differences between the transcriptional signatures of control male and female Cycling NSPCs and suggested that maternal cold stress shifts female Cycling NSPCs toward a more male-like transcriptional profile. Gene ontology analysis revealed that maternal cold stress upregulates pathways linked to neuronal growth, development, and GABAergic neuron differentiation, but only in females. Importantly, ligand-receptor analysis suggested that maternal cold stress exposure disrupts neurodevelopmental programs through altered cell-cell signalling within Cycling NSPCs predominantly in females. These findings demonstrate that prenatal maternal cold stress exposure drives sex-specific effects on fetal neurodevelopment and uncover distinct cellular pathways that may contribute to sex differences seen in the presentation and risk of many NDDs.

observations.text:
BackgroundExposure-history data collected during epidemics or pandemics within digital contact-tracing applications hold immense potential for rapid, scalable epidemiological inference. The sensitivity of these data makes privacy-preserving designs essential to secure public trust and app uptake. However, during the COVID-19 pandemic, such approaches were not yet available at the scale or maturity required for deployment. We present a Bayesian decentralised framework to infer transmission dynamics from exposure-history data while protecting user privacy.

MethodsOur approach is based on iterative communication between user devices and a central server, computing log-likelihood gradients on device from exposure-history data and centrally updating parameter values using only aggregated gradients. Applying this framework to synthetic exposure-history data from a hypothetical respiratory pathogen epidemic simulated on dynamic contact networks, we assessed its ability to estimate the underlying transmission parameters, perform infector attribution, and reconstruct serial-interval (SI) distributions. We systematically explored how inference was affected by incomplete exposure-history data arising from partial app adoption, case under-ascertainment, and incomplete exposure logging, and by transmission scenarios.

FindingsOur decentralised framework accurately recovered transmission parameters, closely matching estimates derived from centralised data with no systematic bias in posterior means. Parameter recovery remained robust when hazards from unobserved exposures were known as a daily average across the population. Although incomplete exposure-history data and specific transmission scenarios introduced compensatory parameter biases, the inferred host infectiousness profile retained sufficient accuracy, and the weekly SI distributions reconstructed from infector attributions closely resembled the ground-truth distributions.

InterpretationOur findings highlight that, beyond its primary role as a control measure, digital contact tracing could help characterise transmission dynamics almost in real time and inform public health interventions while preserving user privacy.

FundingOxford Martin School Programme on Digital Pandemic Preparedness; National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections.

Evidence before this studyWe searched PubMed for studies published from database inception to Sept 30, 2026, using the keywords ("digital contact tracing" OR "exposure notification" OR "contact tracing app") AND ("federated learning" OR "decentralised" OR "privacy-preserving" OR "statistical inference" OR "Bayesian inference") AND ("transmission" OR "serial interval" OR "infectiousness"). During the COVID-19 pandemic, digital contact-tracing (DCT) apps were deployed at an unprecedented scale: 224 COVID-19 apps were launched across 127 countries, 128 of which supported exposure notification. In England and Wales, the NHS COVID-19 app had 16.5 million regular users (28% of the total population) and averted an estimated 1 million cases and 9,600 deaths in its first year. To protect privacy, however, most apps used decentralised architectures that kept exposure-history data on users devices. This privacy-preserving principle has largely prevented these data from being used for epidemiological inference to understand transmission dynamics, such as estimating the serial-interval (SI) distribution and host infectiousness profile over time. While existing decentralised algorithms estimate each users infection risk, we found no study that developed and evaluated a framework for estimating population-level epidemiological parameters from exposure-history data that remain on users devices.

Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first such framework. It estimates key quantities required for understanding transmission dynamics, including how an infected individuals infectiousness changes over time relative to their symptom onset date, how much close contacts increase the risk of transmission, and the SI distribution. The framework learns an exposure hazard function from data that never leave users devices, then attributes infections to likely infectors, and reconstructs the SI distribution. We applied the framework to synthetic exposure-history data from epidemics simulated on dynamic contact networks of 166,034 individuals, matching the 2024 population of Oxford, UK. It produced estimates comparable to those from centralised analysis, identified the timing of peak host infectiousness relative to symptom onset to within one day, and reconstructed SI distributions that closely tracked the ground truth. We also systematically assessed how participation levels (app adoption and case ascertainment), technical limitations (incomplete exposure logging), and surveillance (knowledge of the background hazard from unobserved exposures) affected inference, and showed that daily population-level knowledge of the background hazard was sufficient for reliable inference.

Implications of all the available evidenceBeyond their role as a control measure, DCT apps could provide timely, population-representative estimates of key transmission parameters, such as the host infectiousness profile and SI distribution. Our findings show that such inference is feasible within the privacy-preserving architectures likely to underpin future DCT systems. Greater app adoption, case ascertainment, and exposure logging would improve inference accuracy. To realise this potential, the framework will need to be embedded in DCT systems, supported by concurrent epidemiological research, real-world validation, and early collaboration with public health authorities and platform providers.
observations.title: Privacy-Preserving, Decentralised Inference of Epidemic Transmission Dynamics from Digital Exposure Histories

metadata.summary: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE.  Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Following implant and reperfusion, graft function was assessed over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics.  Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups (HOPE 20h, 86%, HOPE 4h, 81%, and SCS 4h, 77%). Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h (p<0.01), while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed minimal differences in gene and pathway expression among groups.   Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of ischemia in a porcine model, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.

metadata.summary: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and extracellular matrix are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, limits the size of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. Here, we investigated why zebrafish she mutants subsequently develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4–5 days post-fertilization. Before circulatory failure, the mutant DA retained an approximately circular cross-section and showed no detectable changes in the endothelial cell geometry, but exhibited increased distensibility during the cardiac cycle. Mutants had fewer perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein, smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, and reduced col1a1 transcript level. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell numbers, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Ablation of pdgfrb-positive cells largely prevented DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in vascular endothelium. Together, these findings link She function to perivascular fibroblast abundance, fibrillar collagen-gene expression, and arterial stability. They support a model in which impaired perivascular support renders the developing DA susceptible to mural cell-associated collapse, extending the role of She from early vessel-size regulation to maintenance of vascular function.

observations.title: SH2 Domain Protein E sustains perivascular fibroblasts to maintain arterial stability
